title: A New Role for Relevance: Guiding Corpus Interaction in Agentic Search

visual_explainer.question: Once retrieval has bounded the interaction space, can relevance continue to guide the order and visibility of local corpus operations?
visual_explainer.takeaway: RARG carries relevance into DCI execution: document order, entry points, and match-level observations are prioritized rather than treating all files/matches as equally promising.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Raw DCI and bounded interaction-space systems such as RISE/DR-DCI where relevance mostly constructs the workspace.

analysis.tldr: RARG makes relevance an execution prior rather than a one-time candidate filter: it orders document traversal, initializes likely entry points, and reranks local grep matches so limited observation budget reaches useful evidence earlier.
analysis.problem: Raw DCI wastes interaction budget on relevance-agnostic traversal, while bounded workspaces still treat local files and grep matches too uniformly once the candidate set has been constructed.
analysis.core_idea: Use document-level relevance to define traversal order, query-relevant paragraphs to initialize promising entry points, and optional match-level reranking to prioritize local excerpts before they reach the model.
analysis.agent_loop: recall/rank corpus → traverse scoped documents in relevance order → grep locally → prioritize matches → inspect/verify → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: Retrieval scores remain active during interaction rather than only selecting the workspace boundary; relevance controls which local operations and observations get scarce execution/attention budget.
analysis.evidence: On the 100-query BrowseComp-Plus setup with GPT-5.4-mini, RARG++ reports 84% accuracy with 23.9 tool calls versus 78%/28.7 for RISE and 78%/99.1 for DCI. At 1M documents RARG++ retains 79% versus 69% for RISE-BM25. The generative reranking variant is a useful negative: it uses fewer tools but drops to 75%, showing faster convergence is not automatically better search.
analysis.why_it_matters: The DCI lineage evolves from 'remove relevance bottlenecks' to a more nuanced conclusion: relevance is valuable when it guides interaction without collapsing the environment back into fixed top-k evidence delivery.
limitations: Effectiveness depends on embedding quality at both document and local-match granularity.
Order-preserving grep and match reranking add latency, creating a performance-time trade-off.
Evaluation is concentrated on BrowseComp-Plus, four BRIGHT subsets, and GPT-5.x backbones.
